clue.text: Band of gold put on box by artist

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
a chest is a large box
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A gold ring is set on a box by an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a ring of gold, but it is a group of musicians; 'put on' and 'by' just join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony orchestra is a large musical band of players.

clue.text: Imagined monsters and rose about midnight, upset

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go around the next piece
upset tells us the letters of rose are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the middle of the word night is its letter G

explanation.surface: Someone lies awake around midnight, picturing monsters, troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes ORES from ROSE, and 'about' wraps those letters around G, the letter at the very middle of 'night'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are giant monsters of fairy tale, creatures of the imagination.

clue.text: Knocked out, so no cup tickets required

indicators.note: knocked out suggests the letters of so no cup are battered into another shape

explanation.surface: A team knocked out of a cup competition finds its match tickets are no longer needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked out' reads as cup elimination but signals rearranging SO NO CUP; 'required' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Coupons are vouchers or tickets exchanged for goods or entry.

clue.text: Pass one bill in ten after amendment

indicators.note: in places the bill inside the revised letters
after amendment says the word ten has been revised into a new order

parts.note: one account, written A/C, is a bill

explanation.surface: Parliament passes a bill on its tenth reading after amendments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after amendment' rearranges ENT from the clue's ten; 'Pass one bill' reads like parliamentary procedure, but A/C is the accountant's shorthand for an account.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a law is to pass it into statute.

clue.text: A paid informer

parts.note: read not as a police grass but as someone salaried to give pupils information

explanation.surface: Police pay a snitch for tip-offs.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmistress or tutor is paid to inform pupils, passing on knowledge.

clue.text: Insistent it's averse to change

indicators.note: to change tells us the letters of it's averse must be reordered

explanation.surface: A stubborn person is opposed to any alteration.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive apostrophe is ignored; the letters of ITS AVERSE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insistent is forceful and self-confident in pressing a claim.

clue.text: Part of a window dresser's flamboyant attire

definitions.meaning: the sliding frame holding the glass in a vertical window
a showy band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist

explanation.surface: A shop window dresser shows off something flashy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'window dresser' runs across the two definitions as one phrase, hiding the break between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sliding window frame and a decorative band of fabric worn as a garment.

clue.text: Clasp loose on the Spanish knife

indicators.note: loose suggests the letters of clasp come undone and are rearranged

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish knife has a loose clasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges the letters into SCALP; 'Spanish knife' suggests a navaja, but the knife is surgical.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's small, very sharp blade is a kind of knife.

clue.text: All men do

parts.note: do as a noun means a party, so this is a celebration with only men attending

explanation.surface: Every man does it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a verb but is the British noun for a party; a stag party is a pre-wedding night out for the groom and his male friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor's night out before his wedding is a party attended solely by males.

clue.text: Turmoil and ferment heard before laughter

indicators.note: heard means we want what the word for ferment sounds like when spoken

parts.note: to ferment beer is to brew it
ha-ha is laughter

explanation.surface: Unrest and agitation spread before people start laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' signals that BROU is spelt as it sounds, like BREW; 'before' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy commotion or uproar, a state of turmoil.

clue.text: Mark, the sailor, is a six-footer

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A man called Mark, a sailor, is very tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall man but means an insect, which has six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a beetle, and as an insect it has six legs.

clue.text: Provide company car

definitions.meaning: to accompany someone as a guard or companion
the Ford model of that name

explanation.surface: A firm provides a company car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company car' reads as one perk, but splits into two definitions; the Ford Escort was a popular British car.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to accompany someone, and is also the name of a well-known Ford car.

clue.text: Dance band instruments

parts.note: a horn is an instrument played in a band
a pipe is also an instrument heard in a band

explanation.surface: A dance band brings its instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornpipe is a lively solo dance associated with sailors.

clue.text: Took advantage of American in a plot

indicators.note: in places the American abbreviation inside the other piece

parts.note: a bed is a plot of garden ground, so a plot is A BED

explanation.surface: An American in a conspiracy exploited the situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a scheme, but it is a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse a position is to misuse it, exploiting it unfairly.

clue.text: Bring round advance payment? Just joking!

indicators.note: round means bring wraps itself around the payment

parts.note: an ante is a stake paid in advance in poker

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a down payment, then says it was a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' needs no anagram: the word is split as B...RING. 'Just joking!' is a whole-phrase definition of light teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantering is teasing light-heartedly, not being serious.

clue.text: Guard seen changing overalls

indicators.note: changing suggests the letters of guard seen are being swapped round

explanation.surface: A guard is seen changing into work clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' reads as dressing but signals the letters of GUARD SEEN rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are hard-wearing trousers with a bib, a type of work overalls.

clue.text: Mockingbird with tips of tail blue or grey

definitions.note: the verb form used as a noun, the act of mocking

parts.note: the rail is a wading bird

indicators.note: tips of points to the end letters of each following word

explanation.surface: A mockingbird has a tail tipped with blue or grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mockingbird' must be split: 'Mocking' is the definition and 'bird' gives RAIL. 'tips of' takes the last letters of TAIL, BLUE, OR, GREY.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing, the act of making fun of someone.

clue.text: Natural aptitude demonstrated this month in court

parts.note: inst., instant, means of this month in old letter-writing

explanation.surface: A natural flair was shown in court this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) is old business-letter shorthand for 'this month'.
explanation.definitionFit: Instinct is an inborn talent or knack, a natural aptitude.

clue.text: Agreed everything was bound to come out

indicators.note: to come out means the bound word opens up for the other piece

parts.note: tied means bound
all means everything

explanation.surface: Everyone agreed that all of it was bound to come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come out' is a loose container signal: the binding word opens up to admit the other piece. The surface reads as a secret about to emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts that tallied matched up, corresponding or agreeing with each other.

clue.text: Cultivation that's up to date

parts.note: till means up to, as in till Tuesday
an age is a period, a date in history

explanation.surface: Farming methods that are modern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to date' reads as modern but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the ploughing and preparing of land, its cultivation.

clue.text: Hoover, for example, sets me back about £25

indicators.note: about says the turned word goes around the money
back means the word me is read from right to left

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: A vacuum cleaner costs someone about twenty-five pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes EM. The Hoover vacuum takes its name from William Hoover, so a person's name became the thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A word derived from a person's name, like the Hoover vacuum from its maker, is an eponym.

clue.text: Rings about train smash in Canada

definitions.note: a place in Canada, a province

indicators.note: about means the rings go around the next piece

parts.note: two letter O shapes are rings

indicators.note: smash says the word train is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Rings are found around a train crash in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smash' makes NTARI, held between two Os. 'in Canada' is a looser definition: a place found in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is a province located in Canada.

clue.text: Carpet a university residence, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken, giving the answer's sound

parts.note: Keele Hall is the main building of Keele University in Staffordshire, England

explanation.surface: Would one lay carpet in a student residence?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the British verb meaning to reprimand. Keele is an English university, and its hall sounds like the old naval punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To keelhaul someone is figuratively to rebuke them severely, just as being carpeted means a dressing-down.

clue.text: Summer, almost fall

definitions.meaning: one who sums or adds up figures
to stagger unsteadily, nearly falling over

explanation.surface: The end of summer means it's nearly autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is not the season but one who sums; 'fall' looks like autumn too.
explanation.definitionFit: A totter is one who tots up figures, and to totter is to stagger and nearly fall.

clue.text: Image to carry to top of mountain

parts.note: to tote is to carry

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of mountain

explanation.surface: Someone carries a statue up to a mountain summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a carved emblem or figure, a sacred image of a clan.

clue.text: Be quick!

parts.note: quick in its old sense of living, as in the quick and the dead

explanation.surface: Hurry up!
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a command to hurry, but quick here means alive.
explanation.definitionFit: To be among the living is simply to have being, to be alive.

clue.text: Guess what the poet Donne was by profession

definitions.text: what the poet Donne was by profession
definitions.meaning: John Donne was a clergyman, Dean of St Paul's

explanation.surface: Guess John Donne's job.
explanation.walkthrough: John Donne, the 17th-century poet, was Dean of St Paul's Cathedral, a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to guess by insight, and a divine is a clergyman.

clue.text: A bodybuilder showing a heavenly body

parts.note: a steroid builds up the body's muscles

explanation.surface: A muscleman shows off an attractive physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly body' suggests a gorgeous figure, but it is in space.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky object orbiting the sun, a celestial body.

clue.text: Silver-headed editor, getting on a bit

indicators.note: headed means silver comes at the head, before the editor

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A grey-haired editor is growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver-headed' suggests grey hair but means AG put at the head of ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone getting on a bit is elderly, advanced in years.

clue.text: Vessel needing a mast to be at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of a mast to be are muddled

explanation.surface: A ship needs a mast to go to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' reads naturally but signals rearranging A MAST TO BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamboat is a vessel driven by steam power.
